auth.description: PagerDuty REST API access key, sent as the Authorization header after the literal `Token token=`. A read-only key satisfies the four read operations; the two incident writes need a full-access key
auth.name: pagerduty.api_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Create a REST API key in PagerDuty under Integrations, then API Access Keys. A read-only key is enough to list incidents, services and on-calls; acknowledging or resolving an incident needs a full-access key. PagerDuty shows the key once, when it is created
config.label: PagerDuty API access key
config.name: api_token

description: PagerDuty incident response: read incidents, services and who is on call, and acknowledge or resolve an incident

operations.description: List the incidents this key can see, across every service it has access to. Returns one page; read `more` to learn whether another page exists, and page by adding `limit` to `offset`. No status, service, team or time filter is offered by this connector — see pagerduty-incident-get to inspect one incident in full

params.description: Maximum number of incidents to return in this page. PagerDuty caps this at 100
params.name: limit

params.description: Number of incidents to skip before this page begins. To read the next page, add the `limit` just used to the `offset` just used — this is not a page number
params.name: offset

acknowledgements.description: Who has acknowledged the incident and when, each `{at, acknowledger}`. Empty unless status is acknowledged

alert_counts.description: How many alerts rolled up into this incident, `{all, triggered, resolved}`

assignments.description: Who the incident is currently assigned to, each `{at, assignee}` where `assignee` is a user reference

escalation_policy.description: A reference to the escalation policy governing this incident

html_url.description: The PagerDuty web UI URL a human would open

id.description: The incident's own id — pass this as `id` to pagerduty-incident-get, -acknowledge or -resolve

incident_key.description: The deduplication key the triggering integration supplied, when it supplied one

incident_number.description: The account-scoped sequence number PagerDuty displays, distinct from `id`

priority.description: A reference to the account's configured priority level, when the account uses priorities; null otherwise

resolved_at.description: Null until the incident is resolved

self.description: The API URL of this incident

service.description: A reference to the service this incident is on: `{id, type, summary, self, html_url}`. Pass its `id` to nothing here — pagerduty-service-list returns the full representation

status.description: triggered means nobody has taken it; acknowledged means somebody is working it and escalation has paused; resolved is terminal

summary.description: A short human-readable label for the incident, usually its title

teams.description: References to the teams the incident is visible to

urgency.description: Whether the service's escalation policy pages immediately (high) or notifies without paging (low)

limit.description: The limit this page was read with

more.description: True when another page exists past this one. This is the only continuation signal PagerDuty sends — there is no cursor

offset.description: The offset this page was read from

total.description: The total matching incidents. Null unless the request asked for it, which this connector does not

operations.description: Fetch one incident in full, including its current status, urgency, service, assignments and acknowledgements. Read this before acknowledging or resolving, because PagerDuty refuses a status change that does not follow from the incident's current status

params.description: The incident's own id, from pagerduty-incident-list's `id` field. Not the `incident_number` PagerDuty's web UI displays
params.name: id

incident.description: The incident, in the same shape pagerduty-incident-list's array carries

acknowledgements.description: Each `{at, acknowledger}`. Empty unless status is acknowledged

assignments.description: Each `{at, assignee}`, where `assignee` is a user reference

first_trigger_log_entry.description: A reference to the log entry that opened the incident

priority.description: Null unless the account uses priorities

resolve_reason.description: Why the incident was resolved, when it was resolved by being merged into another; null otherwise

resolved_at.description: Null until the incident is resolved

service.description: A reference to the service this incident is on

operations.description: List the services this key can see. A service is what incidents are opened against and what an escalation policy is attached to, so this is how to discover the ids and names behind an incident's `service` reference. Also this connector's connection test

params.description: Maximum number of services to return in this page. PagerDuty caps this at 100
params.name: limit

params.description: Number of services to skip before this page begins. To read the next page, add the `limit` just used to the `offset` just used
params.name: offset

more.description: True when another page exists past this one

acknowledgement_timeout.description: Seconds after which an acknowledged incident re-triggers. Null when an acknowledgement never expires

auto_resolve_timeout.description: Seconds after which an unacknowledged incident auto-resolves. Null when the service never auto-resolves

escalation_policy.description: A reference to the escalation policy this service pages through

integrations.description: References to the integrations that can open incidents on this service

last_incident_timestamp.description: When this service last opened an incident; null if it never has

status.description: The service's current health as PagerDuty sees it: active means no open incidents, warning and critical mean open incidents of increasing urgency, maintenance means a maintenance window is in effect, disabled means the service accepts no new incidents

total.description: Null unless the request asked for it, which this connector does not

operations.description: List who is currently on call, as one entry per escalation policy, escalation level and user. An entry with no `schedule` is a user attached directly to an escalation level rather than through a rotation. Time filtering is not offered by this connector, so this answers `who is on call now`

params.description: Maximum number of on-call entries to return in this page. PagerDuty caps this at 100
params.name: limit

params.description: Number of on-call entries to skip before this page begins. To read the next page, add the `limit` just used to the `offset` just used
params.name: offset

more.description: True when another page exists past this one

oncalls.description: This page's on-call entries. One user can appear more than once — once per escalation policy and level they cover

end.description: When this on-call period ends. Null for a permanent, non-rotating assignment

escalation_level.description: Which level of that policy this entry sits at. Level 1 is paged first

escalation_policy.description: A reference to the escalation policy this entry covers: `{id, type, summary, self, html_url}`

schedule.description: A reference to the on-call schedule that placed this user here. Null when the user is attached to the escalation level directly rather than through a rotation

start.description: When this on-call period began. Null for a permanent, non-rotating assignment

user.description: A reference to the person on call: `{id, type, summary, self, html_url}`, where `summary` is their display name

total.description: Null unless the request asked for it, which this connector does not

operations.description: Acknowledge one incident, on behalf of a named PagerDuty user. This stops the escalation clock and tells the rotation that somebody is working the incident; it does not close it. PagerDuty refuses the change if the incident is already resolved, and answers that as data rather than as a failure

params.description: The incident's own id, from pagerduty-incident-list's `id` field
params.name: id

params.description: The login address of the PagerDuty user this acknowledgement is recorded against. It must belong to a user in this PagerDuty account; PagerDuty answers 400 otherwise. A REST API key carries no user identity of its own, which is why this cannot be inferred
params.name: from_email

incident.description: The incident after the update, in the shape pagerduty-incident-get returns. Read `status` back to confirm the acknowledgement took effect

acknowledgements.description: Each `{at, acknowledger}`; the acknowledger is the user named by the From header

operations.description: Resolve one incident, on behalf of a named PagerDuty user. This closes it: it leaves the open-incident view and notifications stop. If the underlying condition is still live, the next alert opens a brand-new incident rather than reopening this one, so resolve only what is actually fixed

params.description: The incident's own id, from pagerduty-incident-list's `id` field
params.name: id

params.description: The login address of the PagerDuty user this resolution is recorded against. It must belong to a user in this PagerDuty account; PagerDuty answers 400 otherwise. A REST API key carries no user identity of its own, which is why this cannot be inferred
params.name: from_email

incident.description: The incident after the update. Read `status` back to confirm the resolution took effect
